correctness.rationale: With the specified with-replacement update the chain is irreducible for 0<eta,r<1. Reflection at N=4,k=2 gives (a,b,c,b,a). In reset odds h=r/(1-r), the zero and one balances give a/b=(3+eta)/(16(h+eta)) and c/b−1=[16h²+(2+22eta)h+eta(5eta−1)]/[4(1+eta)(h+eta)]. Thus the endpoint comparison requires eta<1/5 and h<(3−15eta)/16; in this eta domain the center comparison has one positive threshold. Substitution in r gives the stated quadratic and discriminant, and at the upper threshold c/b−1=5(1−5eta)/(4(1+eta))>0, proving a nonempty strict interval. Strict maxima cannot be adjacent, so three require at least five counts; the rational example attains this bound. For fixed N the killed zero-noise interior walk is transient; its embedded simple walk Green function is piecewise affine in the start with unit source, and multiplying by the holding time N²/[2j(N−j)] gives the stated rows. The interior resolvent is bounded near (r,eta)=(0,0) with difference O_N(r+eta); boundary injection is O_N(eta), giving O_N(r²+eta) error. The mean uses the exact one-step drift eta(1−2j/N); its stationary limit is k when eta=o(r), yielding boundary masses 1−k/N and k/N. Strict interior Green inequalities on each side of an allowed k persist with o(r) error, while both boundary masses dominate their neighbors. An independent symbolic solution of the full five-state stationary system and exact inverses of the killed chains for N=4 through 12 confirmed the ratios, threshold discriminant, rational example and Green matrix.
residual_risks: The exact window is only for k=2 at N=4; the limiting argument fixes N and requires 2<=k<=N−2. Ties are excluded and no joint N→∞ uniformity is implied.

The Green profile and endpoints explain which probability comparisons sustain three peaks for each fixed larger population and separated reset target, instead of extrapolating from a large-population numerical diagram.
